Area.evidence_source: [012_implications_for_treatment/page/19/Text/2] The results of this study demonstrate that investigating the emotional experiences of adolescents and emerging adults while they are suicidal is integral to enhancing a conceptual understanding of the suicidal state. Increasingly, a focus on emotional experiences may provide valuable insight to assist with the development of treatment strategies that address the disturbing and debilitating negative emotions that contribute to and sustain the suicidal state. [012_implications_for_treatment/page/18/Text/5] As disconnection, alienation, and shame play an integral part in the suicidal experience, encouraging the development of positive emotional resources would be beneficial. [012_implications_for_treatment/page/18/Text/5] Empowering clients to take responsibility for their emotional states through implementing positive life changes and the movement toward more healthy contexts and social interactions is also important. [012_implications_for_treatment/page/18/Text/6] Emotional restructuring is made up of a number of components including emotional arousal, reflection on the arousal for the purpose of integrating reason and emotion, and the promotion of new meaning making that facilitates a reorganization of the client's perception of reality (Greenberg, 2002; Whelton, 2004).
